query: To test whether current neural activity carries information about past behavior, linear decoders (ridge regression) were trained to predict velocity at various time offsets from current neural activity (brown). Performance is the difference in error between actual and control scrambled decoders. Predicted velocity values were averaged over a 10-sec sliding window. Decoders based on current velocity (black) or velocity at all times (gray) are also shown. Shading shows SD across animals.

analyse_plan.Objective: Demonstrate that the brain encodes past velocity (up to at least 20 sec prior) in current neural activity, but does not encode future velocity.
analyse_plan.Validation Checks: Scrambled control destroys temporal relationships; current-velocity-only decoder controls for behavioral autocorrelation; performance = actual error minus scrambled error.
analyse_plan.Steps: 1. Load Data: Load the per-neuron z-scored GCaMP traces, the synchronized velocity time series, and the dataset identifiers for all 14 SWF415 animals; set aside three randomly selected feeding-rich datasets for regularization tuning and use the remaining 11 for evaluation. 2. Define Decoder Targets: For each shifted time offset Δt (-30 s to +30 s), define the decoder target as the average velocity over a 16-timepoint sliding window (~10 s) centered Δt seconds from the current time, after z-scoring velocity. 3. Train Behavior-From-Neurons Decoders: For each Δt, train an elastic-net-regularized linear decoder (L1 + L2) that predicts shifted velocity from current z-scored neural population activity, restricted to velocity-encoding neurons; use 5-fold cross-validation on each dataset with 100-timepoint gaps between train/test segments to prevent leakage; tune the elastic-net regularization on the three set-aside datasets. 4. Train Shuffled Controls: For each Δt, train 50 shuffled-velocity decoders where velocity is circularly shifted by a random amount between 125 and 600 timepoints, discarding shifts that yield a correlation > 0.2 with actual velocity; the average cost of these 50 decoders defines the chance-level performance per Δt. 5. Train Velocity-Only Control Decoders: Train an additional family of decoders that take the animal's current velocity as input (instead of neural activity) and predict shifted velocity, applying the same shifted-velocity baseline; train a separate "perfect" decoder that takes velocity at all times t + Δt, also baselined against its shifted control. 6. Compute Performance Per Δt: Define decoder performance at each Δt as the cost (root-MSE) of the actual decoder minus the average cost of the 50 shuffled-velocity decoders; compute mean and SD of this performance across the 14 animals. 7. Save Key Results: Save the per-animal decoder performance curves for the neural decoder, the current-velocity-only control, and the all-time velocity perfect decoder, together with the across-animal means and SDs used for the panel. 8. Visualization: Plot decoder performance (y-axis) versus Δt (x-axis, -30 to +30 s) for the neural-population decoder (brown), the current-velocity-only control (black), and the all-times velocity perfect decoder (gray), with across-animal SD displayed as shaded bands.

key_analysis_results: The neural decoder (brown) successfully predicted past velocity up to at least 20 seconds prior, exceeding both scrambled and current-velocity-only (black) controls. Future velocity (positive delta_t) was not decodable above the current-velocity baseline.
key_analysis_conclusions: The C. elegans brain retains information about past locomotion velocity (up to 20+ sec) in current activity patterns but does not predict future velocity. This is not simply due to behavioral autocorrelation.

summary_report.abstract: A linear decoder shows current neural activity predicts past velocity (20+ sec) but not future velocity.
summary_report.methods: Ridge regression at temporal offsets -30 to +30 sec; scrambled (brown vs shuffled) and velocity-only (black, gray) controls; n=14 animals. 10-sec sliding window.
summary_report.results: Past velocity decoded up to >=20 sec beyond autocorrelation control. Future not decodable above baseline.
summary_report.discussion: Past-encoding enables computations relating recent actions to current outcomes, relevant for behavioral decision-making.
